component.name: Mutterboard
component.summary: Voice dictation straight to your clipboard

description.p: Press a global shortcut, speak, and get cleaned-up text on your clipboard, pasted into whatever you were typing. Everything runs offline on your own machine — Parakeet for speech-to-text and Qwen for the cleanup pass — so no audio leaves your computer and no API key is needed.

Long dictations work again. The speech model can only take about six and a half minutes of audio in one pass, and anything longer failed with "the local speech model didn't return a result". Long takes are now split at pauses and transcribed piece by piece, and the cleanup pass works through long transcripts in chunks, so twenty minutes of talking comes back cleaned up like a short one. A take that failed this way can be recovered with the retry button in History.

The settings window no longer comes up tiny. Mutterboard has to match the compositor's display scale by hand, and it was reading that number from a file KWin rewrites while you log in — so starting at login could catch it mid-write and land on 1x. It now reads the scale KWin actually applies to X11 windows, and remembers the last good one rather than falling back to 1x.

Cleanup now pins itself to the fastest graphics card instead of taking whichever one the driver happens to list first, and says so out loud when it can only find the integrated one — that silent fallback had been making dictation about fifteen times slower after a system update.

The tray menu can now unload the cleanup model, handing several gigabytes of video memory back to whatever else wants it — a game, typically. Mutterboard loads the model again by itself the next time you dictate, so nothing is lost by unloading it.

Mutterboard is now fully offline. The cloud engine has been removed along with the API key that went with it: dictation runs entirely on your own machine, with Parakeet transcribing and Qwen tidying up. If you already had the local models downloaded, nothing changes except that the engine picker is gone.

The cleanup model is Qwen either way now. The cloud pass had used Meta's Llama 3.3 70B through Groq, which Groq decommissioned on 16 August 2026 — the local Qwen model was already doing the same job just as well, so the cloud half was retired rather than repointed.

Every dictation is now saved to disk — audio and transcript — the moment you stop talking, before anything is sent anywhere. The new History section lists your recent dictations to copy again or re-transcribe from the original recording.

Long recordings are fixed: they no longer get cut off while the audio file is being finalized, are no longer mistaken for silence, and are split automatically when they exceed the engine's limit. Failures now show a desktop notification instead of a message in a window you don't have open, and never delete the recording.
The tray icon turns orange while transcribing and is now symmetrical. The settings header shows the brand waveform without the white tile.
Check for updates and install them from the About section in settings. Removed the "Copied to clipboard" note after dictations.
Fix in-app shortcut rebinding inside the Flatpak sandbox.
First release: cloud and offline dictation, global shortcut, tray, custom vocabulary, recording cues, launch at login.
